questions.question: What's in a Rails app's directory structure?
questions.title: The Rails Directory Structure
questions.direct_answer: A Rails app has a predictable layout: app/ holds your code — models (app/models), controllers (app/controllers), views (app/views), and jobs (app/jobs), mailers (app/mailers); config/ holds routes.rb, environments, database.yml; db/ holds migrations (migrate/) and schema.rb; test/ or spec/ holds tests; Gemfile and Gemfile.lock list dependencies. The app/ folders map to MVC: models, controllers, views. config/routes.rb is the entry point (URLs -> actions). db/migrate/ holds schema changes over time; rake db:migrate runs them. Knowing the layout is how you find where a feature lives — 'where's the Post logic? app/models/post.rb.'

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you can name the key folders (app/models, app/controllers, app/views, config/routes.rb, db/migrate) and what lives in each.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Not knowing where a feature lives (model in app/models, not app/controllers), or putting logic outside the conventional folders.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: app/ (models, controllers, views, jobs); config/routes.rb (entry point); db/migrate (schema changes); Gemfile (deps). Folders map to MVC; convention finds everything.

sections.title: The Layout
sections.content:
app/ (models/controllers/views); config/routes.rb; db/migrate; Gemfile. Folders map to MVC.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[app/models + controllers + views] --> C[config/routes.rb]
  C --> D[db/migrate + schema.rb]
  D --> G[Gemfile + Gemfile.lock]
  G --> T[test/ or spec/]
```

sections.title: The directory structure
sections.content:
```ruby
# A Rails app's layout (convention over configuration):
# app/                        # YOUR CODE
#   models/   post.rb          # data + rules (Post)
#   controllers/ posts_controller.rb  # orchestration
#   views/    posts/show.html.erb     # presentation
#   jobs/     cleanup_job.rb          # background jobs
#   mailers/  user_mailer.rb          # email
#
# config/
#   routes.rb              # URLs -> controller#action (entry point)
#   environments/           # development.rb / production.rb
#   database.yml           # DB config
#
# db/
#   migrate/               # schema changes over time
#     20260808_create_posts.rb
#   schema.rb               # current schema snapshot
#   seeds.rb                # seed data (rake db:seed)
#
# Gemfile / Gemfile.lock    # dependencies
# test/ or spec/            # tests
#
# Find a feature: Post logic -> app/models/post.rb
#   PostsController      -> app/controllers/posts_controller.rb
#   the show page        -> app/views/posts/show.html.erb
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Not knowing where a feature lives (a model is in app/models, not app/controllers).
Putting logic outside the conventional folders (Rails won't find it).
Editing schema.rb by hand (it's generated from migrations; don't).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: app/ holds your code: models, controllers, views, jobs, mailers.
config/routes.rb is the entry point: URLs map to controller#action.
db/migrate/ holds schema changes over time; db/schema.rb is the snapshot.
Gemfile + Gemfile.lock list dependencies; test/ or spec/ hold tests.
The folders map to MVC; knowing the layout is how you find where a feature lives.

sections.content: A Rails app has a predictable layout: app holds your code — models (app slash models), controllers (app slash controllers), views (app slash views), and jobs (app slash jobs), mailers (app slash mailers); config holds routes.rb, environments, database dot yml; db holds migrations (migrate) and schema dot rb; test or spec holds tests; Gemfile and Gemfile.lock list dependencies. The app folders map to MVC: models, controllers, views. config slash routes.rb is the entry point (URLs to actions). db slash migrate holds schema changes over time; rake db migrate runs them. Knowing the layout is how you find where a feature lives — where's the Post logic? app slash models slash post dot rb. A common mistake is not knowing where a feature lives, like a model in app slash models not app slash controllers, and editing schema dot rb by hand, when it's generated from migrations.
